analysis.title: Global Weekly Kickstart: Quality Regains Ground, Momentum Faces Headwinds
key_insights: Global equities face a higher cost of capital. Credit and sovereign spreads are widening, cyclical exposure is being cut, and weaker balance sheets are under pressure.
The Quality long-short pair has risen 12% in the US and 5% in Europe since its September low. GS expects the rotation could continue.
US earnings growth is expected to slow from 30% in 2026 to about 15% in 2027. Europe slows from 20% to below 10%. Higher energy costs pressure margins.
Narrow market breadth adds risk. The gap between headline indices and the median stock can close through a catch-up by laggards or a catch-down by recent winners. Both imply a Momentum reversal.
Quality looks attractive in a catch-down scenario because positioning remains light and valuations are less demanding.
With lower inflation, energy prices and interest rates still the economists' base case, GS favours selective Quality exposure rather than a broad defensive shift.
Global equities fell 1.6% last week as risk appetite deteriorated and Momentum reversed. Technology led the correction, down 7%. EM and Asia fell about 5%.
Europe outperformed last week, supported by lower exposure to AI and its Value characteristics. US 10y yields fell 17bp on the week.
Fed officials are not expected to speak this week because of the blackout period ahead of the FOMC.
GS 12-month forecasts: US 10y at 4.4% from 5.1%, Brent at $75 from $109.9, gold at $5235 from $4180.
GS Bull/Bear Market Indicator stands at 66%. Shiller PE is 40.2 (97th percentile) and unemployment 4.2%.
